subject: Launch Assist: sponsor safety-net / stipend stacking approval request
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Cc: Maria Sanchez <maria@ava-labs.com>
Date: Thu, 15 Mar 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Launch Assist: sponsor safety-net / stipend stacking approval request

Ben, Lauren — looping you in on a small packaging exception request from Ava Labs (Maria copied). They accepted our Launch Assist cohort offer but several of their teams have overlapping sponsor vouchers and our standard sandbox stipend. The ask: allow stacking of sponsor vouchers + sandbox stipend for their April cohort AND permit conversion of up to 30% of unused promotional sandbox credits into a one-time dedicated-discount voucher redeemable within 90 days.

Why: their expected spike in the first 30 days (model fine-tune + evaluations) will push them over the sandbox cap; sponsor wants predictable guardrails instead of ad-hoc top-ups. We flagged this as a potential churn risk if we force an immediate dedicated conversion.

What I need: quick sign-off on two fronts — commercial (is conversion to a dedicated discount allowed from a pricing policy POV?) and ops (can we implement the voucher conversion mechanics and track usage?). I attached their weekly usage report and a term-sheet sketch. If we approve, they want a commit/DocuSign by 03/24 so they can include it in their cohort onboarding emails.

Suggested guardrails: 30% conversion cap, voucher only valid for same billing account, expires in 90 days, non-refundable. We can pair that with a soft telemetry alert for overage risk.

Thanks — Karthik

--
Karthik Iyer
Account Executive, Growth
Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.com

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Launch Assist: sponsor safety-net / stipend stacking approval request

Karthik — thanks for the heads-up and the term sheet. High level: I like the guardrails (30% cap and 90d expiry). Two immediate questions before I can greenlight:

1) Commercial impact: what is the net ARR/TPV delta if we let them convert credits vs. forcing a dedicated commitment? Put another way, is this an early-conversion win or a potential revenue concession?

2) Legal/Tax: converting credits to a voucher that discounts dedicated capacity might have rev-rec or tax implications; need to validate with legal.

Looping Priyom for a quick economics read and Lauren for approvals / revenue ops. If Priyom can give a thumbsup on uplift/impact by EOD tomorrow, I can escalate to pricing committee.

Ben

Quick econ read (numbers below) — happy to discuss on a 15-min call.

Summary: Allowing the 30% conversion into a dedicated-discount voucher looks neutral-to-positive for us because:
- Most accounts redeem <40% of sandbox stipends in the first 90 days; converting a controlled slice reduces our exposure to unmetered burst costs.
- If Ava Labs redeems as a dedicated-discount voucher, we capture margin earlier (applies to committed capacity) vs. unpredictable overage top-ups.

Estimated impact (based on historic Launch Assist cohorts):
- Expected additional committed spend (if they convert voucher to dedicated): $9k-$14k over 3 months.
- Worst-case unilateral voucher redemption without conversion: ~$3k one-off discount impact.

Conditions I recommend for approval:
1) 30% conversion cap (as proposed).
2) Voucher only applied to the billing account tied to the cohort; no cross-account portability.
3) Finance signs off on rev-rec treatment (loop legal if needed).

If Ben still wants pricing committee escalation, I support moving it — but given the relatively modest downside and good customer experience gain, we should approve a pilot.

— Priyom
